♻️ Duplicate comments (2)
tests/integration/incremental_test.go (2)
`35-69`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_ **Incremental archive scoping bug: `findTarArchives(workDir)` returns the initial tar too.** The same `workDir` is used for both `MirrorToDisk` runs. After the second run, the initial `mirror_000001.tar` (with full blob content) typically still sits next to the new incremental `mirror_000002.tar`. Then: - Line 60–61: `incrementalArchives` contains **both** archives. - Line 61: `incrementalBlobCount` sums blobs from initial + incremental, so it will be `>= initialBlobCount`, flipping the `<` assertion at line 64. - Line 69: `expectNoImageBlobsInArchives(incrementalArchives)` will fail because the initial archive holds real layer blobs. This is the same root cause raised in the previous review against the helper functions; the refactor moved the responsibility to the caller, but the caller here doesn't filter to the newest archive. Either snapshot the initial archive list and diff (`incrementalArchives = newMatches \ initialArchives`), or pick the latest tar by mod time before counting.
Suggested fix ```diff By("verifying initial tar archive was produced") initialArchives := findTarArchives(workDir) initialBlobCount := countBlobEntriesInArchives(initialArchives) @@ - By("verifying incremental archive has fewer blobs than initial") - incrementalArchives := findTarArchives(workDir) - incrementalBlobCount := countBlobEntriesInArchives(incrementalArchives) + By("verifying incremental archive has fewer blobs than initial") + allArchives := findTarArchives(workDir) + initialSet := map[string]bool{} + for _, a := range initialArchives { + initialSet[a] = true + } + var incrementalArchives []string + for _, a := range allArchives { + if !initialSet[a] { + incrementalArchives = append(incrementalArchives, a) + } + } + Expect(incrementalArchives).NotTo(BeEmpty(), "no new tar archive produced by incremental run") + incrementalBlobCount := countBlobEntriesInArchives(incrementalArchives) ```
Confirm whether oc-mirror v2 leaves prior `mirror_*.tar` files in place across successive `MirrorToDisk` runs sharing the same working directory: ```shell #!/bin/bash # Look for cleanup or overwrite semantics around mirror_*.tar in the oc-mirror v2 code. rg -nP -C3 '\bmirror_(?:\*|%0)|mirror_%0\d+d|os\.Remove.*mirror_' --type=go rg -nP -C3 'mirror_.*\.tar' --type=go -g '!**/integration/**' ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate. In `@tests/integration/incremental_test.go` around lines 35 - 69, The test uses the same workDir for both MirrorToDisk runs so findTarArchives(workDir) returns both the initial and incremental mirror_*.tar files; update the test around variables initialArchives/incrementalArchives so the second count only inspects the new archive(s) produced by the incremental run (e.g., capture initialArchives, then after the second MirrorToDisk compute incrementalArchives = newMatches minus initialArchives or select the newest tar by modification time) before calling countBlobEntriesInArchives and expectNoImageBlobsInArchives; refer to MirrorToDisk, findTarArchives, initialArchives, incrementalArchives and expectNoImageBlobsInArchives when making the change. ```
--- `33-78`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_ **Missing `SpecTimeout` on this long-running spec.** This It runs two `MirrorToDisk` and two `DiskToMirror` invocations plus registry assertions; without an explicit `SpecTimeout`, a hung oc-mirror call will stall the suite indefinitely.
Suggested fix ```diff - It("should produce a smaller archive on incremental run with --since", func() { + It("should produce a smaller archive on incremental run with --since", func(ctx SpecContext) { By("running initial mirrorToDisk") ... - }) + }, SpecTimeout(20*time.Minute)) ```
As per coding guidelines: "Ginkgo tests should follow quality requirements: ... (3) appropriate timeouts on cluster interactions, flag indefinite waits or missing timeouts".
